verdict.rationale: Community-reported benchmark scores show M5 single-core at 4133 versus about 3679–3748 for M4. One poster attributes the ~10% gain to IPC at the same max clock rather than higher GHz, which fits the story's 'not just a peak-GHz number' framing. However, the scores come from a leaked unboxing video, and nothing shows the M5 *leading* the wider field or translating into instant-feeling interactive work. Missing for 10: comparison against competing CPUs showing single-thread leadership, a verified independent review or benchmark rather than leaked figures, and evidence of real-world interactive responsiveness.

support.subject: As a power-user, everyday interactive work feels instant — leading single-thread performance shown in independent benchmarks, not just a peak-GHz number on a slide

citations.quote: Same max clock speed, ~10% pure IPC improvement with 6MB L2 cache (2MB more than M4).
